rationale: The oil add-on and oil-coupled ultrasound provide indirect pelvic-pain estimates, while the menopause joint-pain comparison was inconclusive. A recovered cancer-treatment trial reports improved aggregate oral symptoms after topical cold-pressed oil plus Solcoseryl. The pain item was unreported. The frozen Parkinson pain direction remains unresolved.

Celery appeared in a mixed Parkinson diet without a separate vocal volume outcome. An earlier homeopathic proving reported hoarseness with other symptoms in a participant, with fresh-leaf identity and low voice volume unverified.

Perilla extracts and inhaled oil showed rodent sleep effects. A perilla-containing tea trial gives inconclusive within-arm sleep-quality changes and no adjusted between-arm estimate. Other combination results remain pending. Dried shiso in Parkinson insomnia remains unresolved.

An original paprika preview summarizes earlier salivary stimulation, with the article outcome pages still gated. Acute oral secretion cannot establish external drooling, and smoked preparation and a Parkinson comparison are unverified.
Ground anise improved SF-36 vitality relative to a declining comparator in functional dyspepsia. Apathy scale data and Parkinson evidence remain unverified.

The ground-anise menopause trial gives no separate insomnia contrast. In another study, the insomnia item declined in both arms receiving a three-oil blend or sunflower oil. This leaves the ground-anise Parkinson direction unresolved.

The mixed-oil transit study provides no clinical constipation outcome. A whole-nut crossover reports no clear bowel-frequency difference and a stool-type difference without direction. Cold-pressed macadamia oil in Parkinson constipation remains unresolved.

A sarcopenia trial family used peanut oil and planned falls surveillance. No arm-specific falls result was recovered. A separate peanut butter trial improved a sit-to-stand test, with inconclusive gait speed and no verified fall-frequency comparison. Neither identifies a refined peanut-oil direction in Parkinson disease.

A topical cold-pressed pumpkin oil combination improved the oral mucositis composite. Speech difficulty was an item and its separate result was unreported. The study provides no listener intelligibility or toasted culinary oil contrast in Parkinson disease.

A pomegranate-peel botanical blend improved a follow-up alertness rating in healthy adults, with an inconclusive omnibus interaction. Juice and rind evidence addresses distinct outcomes. Parkinson seed-oil results remain pending and raw arils have no verified daytime-sleepiness estimate.

The tofu intake study reports an inconclusive Parkinson diagnosis association. Enriched tofu stimulated acute saliva secretion during chewing, with baked preparation and Parkinson drooling outcome unverified.

A Parkinson dark-chocolate crossover gives a one-hour composite motor difference of −0.54 points (95% CI −1.50 to 0.42). Its separate speech-intelligibility estimate was unreported. The registered one-week comparison has no posted results.

Pooled fish intake was associated with lower prevalent smell impairment and an inconclusive opposite-point five-year incidence estimate. Neither result isolates baked cod or Parkinson smell impairment.
